citation: Xue L, Qi H, Zhang H, Ding L, Huang Q, Zhao D, Wu BJ, Li X. Targeting SREBP-2-Regulated Mevalonate Metabolism for Cancer Therapy. Front Oncol. 2020;10:1510. doi:10.3389/fonc.2020.01510.
description: Reviews SREBF2/SREBP-2 as a transcriptional activator of mevalonate and cholesterol-biosynthesis genes, including HMGCR and other pathway enzymes. This directly supports the expectation that Srebf2 loss should decrease sterol-biosynthesis target-gene expression.

citation: Ju D, Zhang W, Yan J, Zhao H, Li W, Wang J, Liao M, Xu Z, Wang Z, Zhou G, Mei L, Hou N, Ying S, Cai T, Chen S, Xie X, Lai L, Tang C, Park N, Takahashi JS, Huang N, Qi X, Zhang EE. Chemical perturbations reveal that RUVBL2 regulates the circadian phase in mammals. Sci Transl Med. 2020;12(542):aba0769. doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.aba0769.
description: Shows that RUVBL2 interacts with BMAL1-containing circadian transcriptional complexes on E-box loci including PER1, PER2, DBP, and NR1D1 in mammalian cells and mice. It supports CLOCK/BMAL1 control of the clock-output genes that fall after Bmal1 or Clock perturbation.

citation: Knoedler JR, Avila-Mendoza J, Subramani A, Denver RJ. The Paralogous Kruppel-like Factors 9 and 13 Regulate the Mammalian Cellular Circadian Clock Output Gene Dbp. J Biol Rhythms. 2020;35(4):378-399. doi:10.1177/0748730420913205.
description: Maps clock-output regulation at Dbp, showing that KLF9/KLF13 modulate CLOCK+BMAL1-dependent Dbp transcription at E-box-proximal sites in mouse hippocampal cells. This supports Dbp as a downstream circadian clock output in neuronal cells.

citation: Hensen SM, Heldens L, van Enckevort CM, van Genesen ST, Pruijn GJ, Lubsen NH. Heat shock factor 1 is inactivated by amino acid deprivation. Cell Stress Chaperones. 2012;17(6):743-755. doi:10.1007/s12192-012-0347-1.
description: Demonstrates that loss of HSF1 DNA-binding activity sharply decreases transcripts of HSF1 heat-shock targets, including HSPA1A, DNAJB1, and HSP90AA1. This supplies a directional expectation for Hsf1 perturbations that reduce Hsp90aa1/Hsph1-family heat-shock genes.

citation: Katoh M. Multi-layered prevention and treatment of chronic inflammation, organ fibrosis and cancer associated with canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling activation. Int J Mol Med. 2018;42(2):713-725. doi:10.3892/ijmm.2018.3689.
description: Reviews APC as a negative regulator of canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling and lists AXIN2 and NKD1 among representative beta-catenin target genes. It predicts that Apc loss should derepress beta-catenin target transcription.

citation: Kosillo P, Doig NM, Ahmed KM, Agopyan-Miu AHCW, Wong CD, Conyers L, Threlfell S, Magill PJ, Bateup HS. Tsc1-mTORC1 signaling controls striatal dopamine release and cognitive flexibility. Nat Commun. 2019;10:5426. doi:10.1038/s41467-019-13396-8.
description: Shows that Tsc1 deletion in dopamine neurons causes constitutive mTORC1 activation and neuronal structural and functional defects that are prevented by reducing Raptor. This supports the direction that Tsc1 loss derepresses neuronal mTORC1 signaling.

citation: Winden KD, Sundberg M, Yang C, Wafa SMA, Dwyer S, Chen PF, Buttermore ED, Sahin M. Biallelic Mutations in TSC2 Lead to Abnormalities Associated with Cortical Tubers in Human iPSC-Derived Neurons. J Neurosci. 2019;39(47):9294-9305. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0642-19.2019.
description: Shows that TSC2 loss in human iPSC-derived neurons activates mTORC1 and, when biallelic, produces transcriptional dysregulation resembling cortical tubers that is partly rapamycin-sensitive. This gives a neuron-specific TSC2-to-mTOR bridge but not a direct prediction for every screen transcript.

citation: Park KK, Liu K, Hu Y, Smith PD, Wang C, Cai B, Xu B, Connolly L, Kramvis I, Sahin M, He Z. Promoting axon regeneration in the adult CNS by modulation of the PTEN/mTOR pathway. Science. 2008;322(5903):963-966. doi:10.1126/science.1161566.
description: Demonstrates that PTEN deletion in adult CNS retinal ganglion cells reactivates mTOR signaling and that Tsc1 deletion similarly promotes axon regeneration. This supports PTEN as a negative regulator of neuronal mTOR but does not name the specific transcripts observed here.

source: Current Topics in Microbiology and Immunology
citation: Aoki M, Fujishita T. Oncogenic Roles of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR Axis. Curr Top Microbiol Immunol. 2017;407:153-189. doi:10.1007/82_2017_6.
description: Reviews activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis by loss of PTEN or TSC1/2 and lists SREBP among mTORC1 downstream effectors. This supplies the indirect bridge from TSC/PTEN loss to lipid-metabolic transcription but not a transcript-level neuronal expectation.

citation: Altaf F, Vesely C, Sheikh AM, Munir R, Shah STA, Tariq A. Modulation of ADAR mRNA expression in patients with congenital heart defects. PLoS One. 2019;14(4):e0200968. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0200968.
description: Identifies FLNB as an ADAR2/ADARB1-edited transcript and reports that Flnb editing is reduced in Adar2-null mouse hearts while total Flnb expression is not detectably changed. This is a specific but nondirectional bridge to the recurrent Flnb abundance decrease in the screen.
